title: Week of June 22–28 · Starter Week
subtitle: Welcome, Camille! Week 1 is calibration — start light, nail your form, and log how each session feels.
goals: Get 3 quality sessions in (Mon/Tue/Wed) — strength, cardio, and mobility
Keep the lifts light this week — RPE 6–7, form first (we'll add load once it's dialed in)
Log weights, reps, and how it felt so next week can build on real numbers
Move easy on the off days — a walk, swim, or stretch keeps things ticking
review: This is your starting point. You're an experienced mover but newer to barbell work, so Week 1 keeps the loads light and the focus on clean technique across a few staple movements. Each lift has a focus cue; pick a weight that feels like a 6–7 out of 10 and stop with a couple reps in the tank. Tuesday is your OrangeTheory-style day — intervals plus core — and Wednesday finishes with mobility. Log everything (even a quick note on how it felt), and next week's plan will progress from what you actually did. Goal trend: a gradual, sustainable move from 135 toward 125 with strength and tone along the way.

days.name: Full-Body Strength A
warmup: 3–4 min easy cardio (walk, bike, or march in place)

items.note: Start light (one dumbbell or kettlebell at the chest), RPE 6–7.
items.focus: Chest tall, sit between your hips, knees track over toes, full depth you can control.

items.note: RPE 6–7 — sub push-ups (on knees if needed) any time.
items.focus: Shoulder blades set, lower under control, press up and slightly together.

items.note: Light — this is a hinge, not a squat.
items.focus: Soft knees, push hips back, feel the hamstrings, flat back the whole way.
Flat back, pull the dumbbell to your hip, squeeze the shoulder blade.
Brace your core, press straight up, don't arch the low back.
Straight line head to heels, squeeze glutes, breathe.
Low back pressed to the floor, move slow and controlled.

days.name: Cardio & Core
warmup: 5 min easy walk or jog to warm up

run.title: Intervals (your OTF-style day)
run.detail: Treadmill or outdoors — your choice. 5 min easy warm-up, then 5 × (1.5 min faster / 90s easy) — 'faster' is comfortably hard, an effort you could hold but wouldn't want to chat through. Finish with 5 min easy. Prefer steady? Run/walk an easy 25 min instead. This is effort-based — no need to chase a number.

hr.main: RPE 7–8 on the faster pushes, RPE 3–4 on recovery
hr.note: Listen to your body — 55+ recovery matters. If a push feels like more than an 8, ease off. Power-walking the intervals counts.

strength.focus: Drive through the heels, squeeze hard at the top.
Reach opposite arm and leg, keep hips level, no rotation.
Stack the hips, straight line, lift tall.
Slow, opposite elbow toward knee, full extension.

days.name: Strength B + Mobility

items.note: Light KB or two DBs, RPE 6–7 — hinge pattern.
items.focus: Hips back, flat back, stand tall by squeezing glutes — don't round.
Step back, drop straight down, tall torso, push through the front heel.
Lead with the elbows, full stretch at the top, control the return.
Control down, press up and together, ribs down.
Hold the KB at your chest, march tall and slow, brace your core.

stretches: Mobility finisher (~8–10 min): World's greatest stretch — 5/side

days.name: Rest / Easy Walk
days.desc: Rest day. Optional: an easy 20–30 min walk to keep the blood moving. Nothing hard — recovery is where the adaptation happens.
fields: Did you move? (walk / swim / nothing — all fine)

days.name: Rest / Mobility or Swim
days.desc: Rest day. Optional: a swim (you enjoy it) or 10 min of gentle stretching. Keep it light and easy.

days.name: Optional Active — Walk / Hike / Swim
days.desc: Free choice, all optional: a hike, longer walk, easy bike, or swim — whatever sounds good and stays enjoyable. Time outside counts double.

days.name: Gentle Yoga / Stretch
days.desc: Gentle yoga or a full-body stretch — hips, hamstrings, shoulders, spine. Restorative and easy; set up the week ahead.
